field_notes.inferred_put_in_coords / inferred_take_o: true when the point was worked out (from directions, geography, or by matching it to an adjacent section's put-in or a named marker) rather than published by a source as that section's put-in/take-out.
field_notes.coord_accuracy: 'as published' = coordinate given by the source; 'high' ~<0.5 km (same named point as a published marker/section); 'medium' ~1-2 km; 'low' ~5 km or worse. Low-accuracy points are for orientation only: confirm on a topo map before relying on them.
field_notes.riverguide put-in: riverguide stores one point per section; spot checks show it is normally the put-in, so it is used as such. A few records may instead point at the access carpark.
field_notes.distance_check: Straight-line put-in to take-out distance compared with the stated section length; SUSPECT flags point to coordinates worth checking.
field_notes.grade_min / grade_max: Numeric parse of the grade text (and hardest rapid) for filtering.
field_notes.hazards: Keyword tags extracted from the description; read the description for detail.
field_notes.deaths: Known fatalities linked to the section. People are not named; see sources. section_match "approximate" means the report did not state the exact section.
field_notes.popularity: 'classic' = well-known, frequently paddled; 'niche' = rarely paddled, exploratory, or packraft-focused; 'standard' = everything else.
field_notes.packraftingtrips grades: Packraft grades, which can differ from hardshell grades.

metadata.safety_disclaimer: River features, wood and access change after every flood. This is a planning aid compiled from public sources, not current beta. Check recent local information, flows and land access before paddling.

deaths.summary: Experienced visiting kayaker (23) died after his kayak wedged between two fallen trees in the swollen Kaituna (Awesome Gorge area of the lower gorges); high water.

Highly experienced kayaker (26) drowned paddling the lower Kaituna downstream of the Trout Pool after becoming separated from her group of three. The coroner recommended a river-users safety forum and exploring log removal.

deaths.summary: Rafting client died after being thrown from a raft at Tutea Falls (reported as a heart attack); a rafting operator later told the coroner a rafter died at Tutea Falls in 2008.

Commercial rafting client fatally injured at Tutea Falls (chest/spinal injuries from a high-energy impact, per the coroner's 2026 findings; initially reported as a medical event). The coroner found the river level and guiding were normal.
Man in his 50s got into difficulty in the Kaituna at the Trout Pool Rd area, Okere Falls, and died at the scene (activity not stated).
